title: Theo and the Witness
premise: Twelve years ago, Wendell Kavanagh testified against the Hollis family in a trial that collapsed when the star witness, Ada Voss, vanished and was declared dead. Now a true-crime podcaster, Wendell has built his quiet life on never being found—until a corpse surfaces wearing clothes lifted from his own closet, a message meant for him alone. As the retrial of patriarch Silas Hollis approaches, Wendell discovers Ada is alive, hidden by the very people sworn to protect her, and that someone inside the case is killing to keep her dead on paper. Racing corrupt deputies, the Hollis heirs, and his own guilt over the testimony he once recanted, Wendell finds Ada and must choose between exposing her—and himself—to save the trial. In the end, Ada testifies, Silas falls, and Wendell trades his invisibility for a life finally witnessed.
about_author: Hazel Iversen is a former court stenographer from northern Michigan who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He records an episode on the cold Voss disappearance, revealing his meticulous filing system and his careful anonymity. A listener email hints someone knows who he is. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine curdling into unease.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Sheriff's deputies summon him to a riverside crime scene: a dead man dressed in clothing stolen from Wendell's closet, a trial transcript page sewn into the lining. Emotional beat: violation—the past has found his address.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Wendell's POV. The original trial, Ada Voss's testimony, its collapse, and Wendell's recanted statement. Emotional beat: shame as the engine of his self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Retrial Notice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Prosecutor Dana Okafor arrives to serve him a subpoena; Silas Hollis's retrial begins in five weeks. She suspects the body is a message. Emotional beat: dread hardening into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: What the Closet Knew
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Searching his own home, he finds a dry-cleaning ticket he never used and a photo of Ada tucked in his coat. Someone has been inside his life for months. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into investigation.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Name
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. The victim is identified as Ray Pell, a former bailiff who signed off on Ada's protective custody. Dana shares sealed files with Wendell, uneasy allies now. Emotional beat: two guarded people choosing cautious trust.

chapters.title: Hollis Country
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He visits the Hollis orchard estate under podcast pretenses; heir Marcus Hollis is charming, menacing, and knows details of the murder not yet public. Emotional beat: the seduction and danger of being seen.

chapters.title: Grave Without a Body
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He digs into Ada's official death record and finds the coroner's signature belongs to a doctor who died before the date on the certificate. Emotional beat: the thrill of the first real crack.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Cried Wolf
chapters.summary: Deputy Corliss's POV. A crooked deputy warns Wendell off, then is found beaten after their meeting—a warning meant to look like Wendell's doing. Emotional beat: the frame tightening around him.

chapters.title: Suspect Number One
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Wendell is briefly detained; his alibi is his own secret surveillance habit, which he must confess to escape charges. Emotional beat: humiliation traded for survival.

chapters.title: Letters to a Ghost
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following the dry-cleaning trail, he finds a storage unit of unsent letters addressed to him in Ada's handwriting—she has been watching him too, for years. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through fear.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, first appearance. Hidden in a lakeside convent, Ada reveals she faked her death when the marshals' leak got Ray's predecessor killed. She refuses to testify. Emotional beat: love and duty colliding across a kitchen table.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Invisible
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Wendell compare twelve years of hiding; she confesses she chose silence partly to protect him from what she saw the night of the murder. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared damage.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Marcus offers Wendell money and the story of a lifetime if the podcaster buries the retrial; Wendell secretly records it. Emotional beat: temptation met with a spine he didn't know he had.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. The safehouse location leaks through the prosecutor's office; the convent burns. Ada escapes into the woods, wounded. Emotional beat: betrayal at the highest level, panic in the dark.

chapters.title: The Man in the Woods
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hunted through the orchard country at night, Ada kills one of Marcus's men in self-defense and realizes the killer in borrowed clothes was sent to stage her 'return.' Emotional beat: survival's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell airs the Marcus recording, torching his podcast career and anonymity in one broadcast, and names the leaked source: Chief Deputy Brandt. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full view.

chapters.title: Brandt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana arrests Brandt, whose ledger reveals twelve years of Hollis payments—including to the marshal who 'buried' Ada. The conspiracy unspools. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by how deep the rot ran.

chapters.title: Before the Judge
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Eve of testimony: Ada, bruised and hunted, decides to walk into the courthouse alive rather than stay dead and safe. Wendell stands witness to her choice. Emotional beat: love expressed as letting her go.

chapters.title: The Witness Speaks
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. On the stand, Ada identifies Silas and exposes the staged-death operation; Marcus attempts intimidation in the gallery and is taken down when Wendell's recordings play. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into power.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Silas is convicted; Marcus cuts a deal that implicates the last protectors; Brandt pleads out. Wendell closes the podcast with his own name and his own testimony, on record at last. Emotional beat: grief and relief braided together.

chapters.title: Witnessed
chapters.summary: Ada and Wendell's POV, alternating. Months later, they meet without aliases at the rebuilt orchard gate; Ada plants a tree where the body was found. Two people step out of hiding together. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, love chosen openly.
